title: Completion of a finite ideal and its residue generator space
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be a finitely generated ideal, and let $c:R\to S=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}R/\mathfrak m^n$ be the canonical completion map [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Put $J=IS$, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mS$ and $k=R/\mathfrak m$, and use the canonical residue-field identification $S/\mathfrak n\cong k$. Give $I^\wedge=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}I/\mathfrak m^nI$ its $S$-module structure by coordinatewise multiplication. Completion of the inclusion $I\hookrightarrow R$ induces an $S$-linear isomorphism $\alpha:I^\wedge\xrightarrow{\sim}J$, carrying the compatible classes of $a\in I$ to $c(a)$. It satisfies $\alpha(\mathfrak m I^\wedge)=\mathfrak nJ$, where $\mathfrak m I^\wedge$ is the $R$-submodule generated by the products $ay$, $a\in\mathfrak m$, $y\in I^\wedge$. The map $I/\mathfrak mI\to J/\mathfrak nJ$, $a\bmod\mathfrak mI\mapsto c(a)\bmod\mathfrak nJ$, is an isomorphism of $k$-vector spaces.

source.place: Tags 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), parts (2) and (3), and 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), part (2), applied to the inclusion of an arbitrary finite ideal and reduction modulo the maximal ideal.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules] to $0\to I\xrightarrow{u}R\to R/I\to0$, with completion ideal $\mathfrak m$. These are finite $R$-modules: $I$ is finite by hypothesis and the other two are cyclic. Thus the completed inclusion $f=u^\wedge:I^\wedge\to S$ is injective and $S$-linear for the specified coordinatewise actions. On the compatible classes $\iota_I(a)$ it has value $c(a)$, directly from the coordinate formula for $u^\wedge$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor], every $y\in I^\wedge$ is a finite sum $\sum_j s_j\iota_I(a_j)$ with $s_j\in S$ and $a_j\in I$. Hence $f(y)=\sum_j s_jc(a_j)\in IS$. Conversely each element of $IS$ is such a finite sum and equals $f(\sum_j s_j\iota_I(a_j))$. Therefore $\operatorname{im}f=J$. Corestricting the injective $S$-linear map $f$ to this image gives the required isomorphism $\alpha:I^\wedge\to J$ and its asserted formula.

source.place: Tag 00MA, lemma-completion-tensor, part (3), canonical tensor map

proof.text: By $R$-linearity and surjectivity of $\alpha$, its image on $\mathfrak mI^\wedge$ consists exactly of finite sums $\sum_j c(b_j)z_j$ with $b_j\in\mathfrak m$ and $z_j\in J$. This is $\mathfrak nJ$: expanding an element of $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mS$ introduces terms $c(b)s z=c(b)(s z)$ with $s z\in J$, and the reverse inclusion uses $c(b)\in\mathfrak n$. Thus $\alpha(\mathfrak mI^\wedge)=\mathfrak nJ$.

The ideal $\mathfrak m$ is finite by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] with completion ideal $\mathfrak m$, module $I$, and exponent $1$. The first-coordinate map induces an $R$-linear isomorphism $p:I^\wedge/\mathfrak mI^\wedge\to I/\mathfrak mI$. Its inverse sends $[a]$ to $[\iota_I(a)]$, since the first coordinate of $\iota_I(a)$ is $[a]$. The isomorphism $\alpha$ and step 3 induce an isomorphism $\bar\alpha:I^\wedge/\mathfrak mI^\wedge\to J/\mathfrak nJ$; explicitly its inverse is induced by $\alpha^{-1}$, because step 3 identifies the submodules. Thus $\bar\alpha p^{-1}$ sends $[a]$ to $[c(a)]$ and is bijective. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal], with ideal $\mathfrak m$, the identification $S/\mathfrak n\cong R/\mathfrak m$ carries the class of $c(r)$ to $[r]$. Consequently this $R$-linear map is $k$-linear: for $[r]\in k$, $[c(ra)]=[c(r)c(a)]$. This proves precisely the stated residue generator isomorphism.

lean.statement: theorem exists_completedIdeal_generatorFibre {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≤ maximalIdeal R) (hIfg : I.FG) : ∃ α : AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) I ≃ₗ[AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R] I.map (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R)), (∀ y : AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) I, (α y : AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R) = map (maximalIdeal R) I.subtype y) ∧ (∀ a : I, (α (of (maximalIdeal R) I a) : AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R) = algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R) (a : R)) ∧ α '' (↑(maximalIdeal R • (⊤ : Submodule R (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) I)) : Submodule R (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) I)) : Set (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) I)) = (↑((maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R)) • (⊤ : Submodule (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R) (I.map (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R))))) : Set (I.map (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R)))) ∧ ∃ e : (R ⧸ maximalIdeal R) ≃+* (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R ⧸ (maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R))), (∀ s : AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R, e.symm (Ideal.Quotient.mk ((maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R))) s) = evalOneₐ (maximalIdeal R) s) ∧ ∃ β : (I ⧸ (maximalIdeal R • (⊤ : Submodule R I))) →ₛₗ[e.toRingHom] ((I.map (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R))) ⧸ ((maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R)) • (⊤ : Submodule (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R) (I.map (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R)))))), Function.Bijective β ∧ ∀ a : I, β (Submodule.Quotient.mk a) = Submodule.Quotient.mk (α (of (maximalIdeal R) I a))

reviewed_lean.note: Clause-by-clause match. α is S-linear and fixed by agreeing with AdicCompletion.map m I.subtype; it sends of a to c(a). α maps the R-submodule m•⊤ onto n•⊤ in J (true because n = span_S c(m)). e : R/m ≃+* S/n is fixed by e.symm(mk s) = evalOneₐ s and exists by ker_evalOneₐ_eq_map since m is finitely generated. β is bijective, semilinear along e and sends [a] to [α(of a)] = [c(a)], so no map is arbitrary.
